item.title: Children in King’s Lynn receive surprise books and bears
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Children in King’s Lynn receive surprise books and bears
Youngsters attending a Munchkin and Me session in King’s Lynn have received a surprise gift of teddy bears and reading packs. The items were donated by the Build-A-Bear Foundation and the charity BookTrust as part of a national gifting initiative.
Each child was given a bear to act as a reading companion, alongside a pack containing books and activities. The donation is part of the Bookstart programme, which aims to support families in sharing stories together. Organisers hope the gifts will encourage children to develop a love of reading and help parents incorporate storytelling into their daily routines. Around 1,000 bears have been distributed to children across the UK through this partnership.

item.title: King’s Lynn marks start of festive season
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn marks start of festive season
More than 1,500 people gathered in King’s Lynn’s Tuesday Market Place on Sunday for the town’s annual Christmas lights switch-on. The event featured an afternoon of live entertainment, including performances from the St Martha’s School Choir, the band Above All Else, and singer Sarah Mai.
West Norfolk Mayor, Councillor Steve Bearshaw, officially illuminated the town’s festive displays at 5pm. Organised by West Norfolk Council, the celebration was hosted by Jeremy Durrant. Local officials have thanked the performers and the public for attending the event, which marked the official start of the countdown to Christmas in the town.

New coffee shop to open in King’s Lynn
A new branch of Esquires The Organic Coffee Co. is scheduled to open in King’s Lynn this Wednesday, November 25. The café is located on the High Street at the site of the former Burtons and Coneys menswear store.
Signage has been visible at the premises for several weeks, and preparations are now nearing completion with furniture and lighting installed. The franchise, which already operates a site in Swaffham, specialises in organic and Fairtrade coffee. This opening follows the brand’s announcement in October that it would be expanding into the town.

item.title: Murder investigation launched in Wisbech
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Murder investigation launched in Wisbech
Police remain at a property on Alexandra Road in Wisbech following the death of a 61-year-old woman. Officers were called to the scene at approximately 9:50pm on Saturday. A 62-year-old man was arrested at the location on suspicion of murder and is currently in police custody.
Detective Inspector Andrew Moralee of the major crime unit has described the event as an isolated incident and confirmed that officers are not searching for anyone else. Residents with information are encouraged to contact the police online or by calling 101, quoting Operation Emeth. Investigations at the site are ongoing.

item.description:

West Norfolk students showcase musical talents at Marshland High School
Marshland High School in West Walton has hosted an annual musical workshop for students across the West Norfolk Academies Trust. Fifty-two pupils, including 41 from primary schools and 11 from the host secondary school, spent the day developing their skills on brass, woodwind, string, and piano instruments.
The event saw a 20 per cent increase in participation compared to last year. Students worked in wind and string ensembles before performing for families in the school hall. Organisers say the initiative aims to build confidence and teamwork, providing young musicians with opportunities to apply skills learned during their weekly lessons. The workshop is part of a wider programme that rotates annually between the trust’s various high schools.

item.title: Construction begins on new £24 million Wisbech school
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Construction begins on new £24 million Wisbech school
Work has officially started on a new £24 million secondary school in Wisbech. Being built by Henry Brothers on the grounds of the Thomas Clarkson Academy, the facility will provide 600 places for students in years seven to eleven. The school will be managed by the Brooke Weston Trust and is designed to address the rising demand for secondary education in the area.
The development features sustainable design elements, including a bio-solar roof and photovoltaic panels to improve energy efficiency. The project was procured through the Department for Education construction framework and is expected to provide a modern learning environment for the growing local community.

item.title: West Norfolk schools support Children in Need
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
West Norfolk schools support Children in Need
Pupils and staff across the West Norfolk Academies Trust took part in fundraising activities for BBC Children in Need on Friday, November 13. Schools in Hunstanton, King’s Lynn, Clenchwarton, Heacham, and Walpole Cross Keys joined the national appeal by swapping uniforms for yellow, spots, and Pudsey Bear ears.
Participants engaged in various classroom activities, games, and assemblies to learn about the charity’s work supporting disadvantaged children. Schools involved included Smithdon High, Heacham Infant and Nursery, West Lynn Primary, Clenchwarton Primary, and Walpole Cross Keys Primary. Families were encouraged to contribute to the cause through digital donations, with staff highlighting the importance of teaching students about responsibility and supporting those in difficult situations.

Busy month of community projects for Priory Rotary Club
The Priory Rotary Club has completed a series of community projects across the King’s Lynn area. Volunteers recently planted a new oak tree and created a wildflower bed at Wootton Park. The club also hosted its annual technology tournament for students from five local schools, and served a harvest lunch to 80 elderly residents in Dersingham.
Financial support has also been provided to several charities, including the Tapping House hospice and the Fairstead Community Shop. Looking ahead, the club is preparing for its annual Swimarathon, scheduled for February 6 at St James Pool in King’s Lynn. Those interested in joining the club or learning more about their upcoming events can visit the Priory Rotary website.

item.title: Queen Elizabeth Hospital specialist wins national mentoring award
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Queen Elizabeth Hospital specialist wins national mentoring award
A health play specialist at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn has been honoured with a national award. Nicola Wright received the Starlight Mentor of the Year Award 2026 at a ceremony in London on November 10. The accolade recognises her work in training the next generation of specialists who use therapeutic play to support children through medical treatment.
Ms Wright was nominated by her apprentice, Claire Burrell, who credited her mentor with building the confidence needed to succeed in the role. The hospital’s play team works across the Rudham ward, helping young patients manage fears surrounding procedures and long-term hospital stays. Chief nurse Dawn Collins praised Ms Wright for her dedication to both patient care and staff development.

Murder investigation launched in Wisbech
Police have opened a murder investigation following the death of a 61-year-old woman in Wisbech. Officers were called to a property on Alexandra Road at approximately 9:50pm yesterday evening, where the woman was found deceased. A 62-year-old man was arrested at the location on suspicion of murder and remains in custody.
Detective Inspector Andrew Moralee of the Major Crime Unit has described the event as an isolated incident and confirmed that police are not seeking any other suspects. Specialist officers remain at the scene to continue their enquiries. Anyone with information regarding the case is asked to contact the police via 101 or their website, quoting Operation Emeth.

We take a look back at a long-standing career at the Campbell’s soup factory in King’s Lynn. In November 1996, Ken Durrant of Gaywood retired after 37 years of service. Mr Durrant was one of the first employees at the Hardwick Road site and spent 22 of those years working in the security hut. He was one of only two staff members to reach such a milestone at the company. Mr Durrant was joined by his wife and family for a farewell presentation with his colleagues to mark the end of his lengthy career.

Birmingham teenager sentenced following Lynn nightclub incident
A 19-year-old man from Birmingham has been handed a six-month conditional discharge after admitting to being drunk and disorderly in King’s Lynn. Brayden Tonks was arrested in the early hours of October 17 following a confrontation with door staff and police on Norfolk Street.
During the incident at 2:45am, Tonks swore at officers and behaved aggressively. Appearing before Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, Tonks apologised for his actions and promised the court it would not happen again. In addition to the conditional discharge, he was ordered to pay £40 in court costs and a £26 victim surcharge.

item.title: Norfolk councillors scrutinise hospital service review
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Norfolk councillors scrutinise hospital service review
Norfolk County Council’s Health Overview Scrutiny Committee has examined a new ‘Case for Change’ report from the Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group. The review outlines potential service adjustments at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn, citing workforce shortages and a projected £53 million deficit by 2034.
Councillors raised concerns that proposed changes could force West Norfolk residents to travel to Norwich for care. During the meeting, Councillor Alexandra Kemp warned that longer travel times on the A47 could negatively impact patient outcomes. While no final decisions have been made, the committee has called for greater transparency and clarity regarding the potential impact on local families and the wider healthcare system.
